To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a piezoelectric plate can be used to harvest energy from a fluid flow, that the energy harvesting can be optimized by choosing the correct internal and external electrical impedance, and that energy harvesting can be enhanced by increasing the number of piezoelectric elements.
the piezoelectric flag is a good candidate for energy harvesting in a flow.
the fluid–solid-electric energy transport in a piezoelectric flag can be enhanced by the presence of an external electrical load.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and application of mathematical and computational models of fluid-structure interaction (FSI) problems, with a particular emphasis on the modelling and simulation of fluid-elastic energy harvesting systems.
the study of the fluid-solid-electric energy conversion in a flexible plate equipped with a piezoelectric patch.
the study of the fluid–solid–electrical dynamics of a flexible structure covered by interconnected piezo-electric patches in an external steady flow.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the piezoelectric flag energy harvester can be used to harvest energy from fluid flows, and the energy conversion efficiency of this system depends on the electrical load, the flow velocity, and the geometry of the piezoelectrics.

the energy harvesting of a fluid–solid system can be improved by using an internal electrical circuit, but only if the electrical circuit impedance is properly tuned with respect to the mechanical one.
the electric network has a positive effect on the energy harvesting performance, but the effect is strongly dependent on the electrical network topology and on the electrical network parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the piezo-electric flag can harvest more energy when the electrical impedance of the circuit is high and the mechanical damping is low.

a piezoelectric plate can harvest energy from a fluid flow by using the fluid–solid coupling as a source of mechanical energy and converting it into electrical energy through the piezoelectric coupling.
the fluid–solid coupling and the electric circuitry are both essential to achieve the maximum power output of the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the presence of an electric load, the energy conversion from fluid to solid and solid to electric can be controlled by the relative position of the patches along the plate.

, for a given external circuit, a piezoelectric flag with a single internal electrical circuit can harvest more power than a piezoelectrical plate with multiple electrical networks, provided that the internal circuit is designed properly.
a piezoelectric plate can be designed as an energy harvester with a very large bandwidth and with a maximum power output comparable to that of a single piezoelectric element.
